stories.headline: Where do 2026 champion Valkyries rank among every WNBA title team?
stories.summary: Las Vegas' 2023 title team topped our rankings two years ago. Where do the 2026 Valkyries fit in?
stories.body:
On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA title in just their second year to put the finishing touches on the league's 30th season. Where do they rank among all of the WNBA champions?

The Valkyries built their reputation on being a complete team that relied on defense. At 67.4 points per game, they had the lowest scoring average in the Finals of any champion since Sacramento (66.8 PPG) in 2005. Golden State is also one of just five WNBA champions that averaged fewer points in the WNBA Finals than the team it defeated for the title.

But the Valkyries lit up the Bay Area Halloween celebrations with their thrilling second-half comeback victory in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals. The league went to a best-of-seven format for the Finals in 2025, but this year was the first to go the distance. The No. 2 seed Valkyries won three times at home at Chase Center in the series and once on the road at State Farm Arena.

Gabby Williams, in her first year with Golden State, was the Valkyries' go-to player who performed offensively at a superstar level in the postseason. She averaged 21.0 points in 13 playoff games, including five of 25 points or more. Her 30 points in Game 7 helped secure the WNBA Finals MVP award. In those seven games, she averaged 19.6 points, which ranks 19th among the 30 Finals MVPs.

The Valkyries did it their way: 100% committed to defense and a process that worked all season. And even though they don't rank in the top 10 all time, being anywhere on this list is great because these teams are all the ultimate winners.

1. 2023 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 34-6, 8-1

Defeated the New York Liberty 3-1 in Finals

As good as they were in winning the 2022 championship, the Aces were even better in 2023. They ranked No. 1 in scoring and defense during the Regular-season and stumbled just once in the playoffs, in Game 3 of the Finals. A'ja Wilson got her first WNBA Finals MVP honor for her performance in 2023; she won again for the 2025 Finals.

In Chelsea Gray, Kelsey Plum and Jackie Young, the Aces also had trio of guards who were among the best backcourts in league history.

Candace Parker, a free agent signee who was expected to be a big part of the Aces' 2023 title run, was sidelined by foot surgery that July. The Aces also lost starters Gray and Kiah Stokes before Game 4 and still won the title, illustrating how good the chemistry was for the team. The Las Vegas bench -- then led by Alysha Clark, Cayla George, Sydney Colson and Kierstan Bell -- came through when they were needed most.

2. 2000 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-5, 6-0

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-0 in Finals

This was the last of Houston's four consecutive title teams, the end of the Comets' version of "Camelot." In 2000, the WNBA was at 16 teams and most of the former ABL players were in their second year in the league. Sheryl Swoopes won her first of three MVP awards and two-time MVP Cynthia Cooper played her last full season at age 37.

As was the case with the other Houston championship teams, the stars carried them: Swoopes and Cooper averaged 35 minutes a game, Tina Thompson 34 and Janeth Arcain 30.5. Fifth starter, Tiffani Johnson (22.2), was the only other player who averaged at least 20 minutes a game. With three future Hall of Famers (Cooper, Swoopes, Thompson), Houston didn't need much statistically from its reserves. The Comets' bench players knew their roles, and the team knew how to win. This title ended the dynasty -- the Los Angeles Sparks were ascending -- but what a finish.

3. 2020 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 18-4, 6-0

Defeated the Las Vegas Aces 3-0 in Finals

Point guard Sue Bird, part of all four Storm title teams, has ruminated over which of them was "best." Lauren Jackson was the superstar of the 2004 and 2010 Storm title teams; her counterpart in 2018 and 2020 was Breanna Stewart. Bird said an edge goes to the very similarly constructed 2018 and 2020 teams due to the presence of guard Jewell Loyd. Bird then gives a nod to the overall depth and chemistry to the 2020 Storm, who were first in the league in offensive and defensive rating.

"The way we shot 3's, the way we moved the ball -- if you took something away, we'd just keep it moving," Bird said. "We talked before every game that we were going to wear teams out with the pace that we played."

4. 2013 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 7-0

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

This was the second of four Lynx titles in a seven-season span. They didn't have the best regular-season record among Lynx champs; both 2011 and 2017 went 27-7 (and the 2016 runners-up were 28-6). But coach Cheryl Reeve said the "core four" of the franchise -- Seimone Augustus, Rebekkah Brunson, Maya Moore and Lindsay Whalen -- were near the peak of their collective powers in 2013. They all averaged double figures in scoring, led by Moore's 18.5 PPG. The fifth starter was Janel McCarville, Whalen's former University of Minnesota teammate, and that pairing again thrilled Gophers fans.

In 2012, Minnesota lost 3-1 in the Finals to Indiana, which irked the Lynx because they were five games better than the Fever in the regular-season standings. The 2013 team didn't allow any openings in the playoffs, sweeping Seattle, Phoenix and Atlanta.

5. 1998 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-3, 4-1

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 2-1 in Finals

Cooper said if she had to pick just one Comets championship team as her favorite, it would be this one. The team's .900 winning percentage (27-3) remains the best in WNBA history. Swoopes was second on the team in scoring at 15.6 PPG to Cooper's 22.7. Cooper won her second consecutive MVP award; she was Finals MVP for all four championship teams.

And there's another reason this team is dear to Cooper's heart. Her close friend, Kim Perrot, the Comets' spark plug point guard, averaged 8.5 points and 4.7 assists in what would be her last season in the WNBA. Perrot had 13 points, five rebounds and four assists in the title-clinching win over the Mercury. Five months later, she was diagnosed with cancer and died in August 1999 at age 32.

6. 2014 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 29-5, 7-1

Defeated the Chicago Sky 3-0 in Finals

Amid the Lynx dynasty from 2011 to 2017, the Mercury owned this season. Their 29 wins was a WNBA record at that time, and they were first in offensive and defensive rating. All five starters -- Diana Taurasi, Brittney Griner, Candice Dupree, Penny Taylor and DeWanna Bonner -- averaged double digits in scoring.

Their only loss in the playoffs came to Minnesota in Game 2 of the Western Conference finals, but they bounced back to win the series with an 18-point Game 3 victory. In the WNBA Finals, Chicago was no match. Taurasi, who averaged 16.2 PPG in the Regular-season and 21.9 PPG in the playoffs, was WNBA Finals MVP for the second time.

7. 2017 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-7, 6-2

Defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 3-2 in Finals

Minnesota was still smarting over a 3-2 Finals loss to Los Angeles in 2016, and the teams were again archrivals in 2017. Minnesota was first in the league in offensive and defensive rating and Los Angeles was second in both.

Target Center was being renovated, so the Lynx's home games in the 2017 playoffs were at the University of Minnesota' Williams Arena, where Whalen had played in college. The decisive 85-76 Game 5 win came in a packed and cacophonous Williams, and Fowles was Finals MVP for a second time (she also won in 2015).

8. 2019 Washington Mystics

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-3

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-2 in Finals

Elena Delle Donne said this was the best team she has ever played on: "Not just talent-wise, but the way emotionally and mentally we were so on-point with one another. That's what took us to the next level."

The Mystics were more dominant in the Regular-season than the playoffs, but had to overcome a back injury that hampered Delle Donne during the Finals. She was the MVP in 2019, but teammate Emma Meesseman was the Finals MVP, averaging 17.8 points in the championship series.

9. 2022 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 26-10, 8-2

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-1 in Finals

The 2022 Aces ran into more challenges in the Regular-season than the 2023 version of Las Vegas. But by the playoffs, they were in control as the league's best team.

In coach Becky Hammon's first season with the franchise, the Aces changed their playing style -- 3-pointers became a far bigger part of the offense -- and Plum and Young matured into even better players. Wilson won her second regular-season MVP award and was Defensive Player of the Year. Then Gray was on fire throughout the playoffs, winning Finals MVP.

It was a big achievement for a franchise that started when the league did in 1997, in Utah, moved to San Antonio, and then found its championship home in Las Vegas under owner Mark Davis. He paid top dollar to bring Hammon from the NBA, where she was a San Antonio Spurs assistant, and it was a great investment.

10. 1999 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-6, 4-2

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-1 in Finals

In 1999, almost all the former ABL standouts had transitioned into and strengthened the WNBA. That didn't stop the Comets, who added former ABL player Sonja Henning at point guard. Houston's standouts were the same as in 1998: Cooper, Swoopes and Thompson. Bulgarian center Polina Tzekova, then 31, made the most of her only WNBA season, starting every game for Houston in 1999.

Ultimately, there was a melancholy feel to the 1999 championship for the Comets. Their former point guard Perrot died from cancer on Aug. 19. After being stunned by Liberty guard Teresa Weatherspoon's buzzer-beating halfcourt heave in Game 2 of the Finals, Houston won Game 3 and secured its third title in honor of Perrot.

11. 2024 New York Liberty
Regular-season and playoff records: 32-8, 8-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-2 in Finals

It took 27 years since the launch of the Liberty as an original WNBA franchise in 1997, but New York finally broke through for its first championship. After finishing with the best record in the league, the Liberty defeated defending champion Las Vegas in the semifinals and then avenged a Commissioner's Cup final loss to Minnesota in the Finals.

The deciding Game 5 vs. the Lynx nearly extended the Liberty's long postseason heartbreak. But a late foul (still disputed by Minnesota) sent Breanna Stewart to the line. She scored the tying points to send the game into overtime, where New York prevailed 67-62.

Jonquel Jones won the Finals MVP honor as she got her first title. Sabrina Ionescu also won the championship for the first time. It was the third title for Stewart, who won two championships in Seattle.

12. 2001 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 28-4, 6-1

Defeated the Charlotte Sting 2-0 in Finals

The Sparks learned a lot going against Houston for four seasons before making their championship breakthrough. Los Angeles star Lisa Leslie has joked, "Thank God that Coop retired," in reference to the Houston's Cooper ending her playing career after the 2000 season (she returned for four games in 2003 at age 40).

Leslie, Mwadi Mabika, Tamecka Dixon and DeLisha Milton-Jones all averaged in double figures during this title run. Leslie was MVP for the season and the Finals.

13. 2011 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-7, 7-1

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

In 2010, Minnesota got a new coach (Reeve) and also added Whalen (trade) and Brunson (Sacramento dispersal draft). The next year brought the opening championship of the Lynx dynasty as No. 1 pick Moore was Rookie of the Year. The 22-year-old Moore started alongside Taj McWilliams-Franklin, who turned 41 two weeks after the Finals ended. This Lynx team really spanned the age/experience gamut.

The season also brought a well-deserved spotlight to Augustus, who became the original building block for the dynasty when she was drafted No. 1 in 2006. She led the 2011 Lynx in scoring in the Regular-season (16.2) and playoffs (22.0) and was the Finals MVP.

14. 2016 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-2 in Finals

After winning back-to-back titles in 2001-02, the Sparks endured a lot of frustrating "almost" in the playoffs. They lost in the WNBA Finals in 2003 and the conference finals in 2006, 2008, 2009 and 2012. The playoff format changed in 2016, seeding the top eight teams regardless of conference, and the Sparks made the Finals again. In an epic five-game series, they beat Minnesota 77-76 on Nneka Ogwumike's putback with 3.1 seconds remaining. Ogwumike was the season MVP and teammate Candace Parker the Finals MVP. It was the last jewel to complete Parker's crown; she already had won two NCAA titles and two Olympic gold medals.

15. 2025 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 30-14, 9-3

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 4-0 in Finals

The 2025 Aces might be the most difficult champion to rank because the first half of their five-month season (counting playoffs) was so different from the second half. But some key factors elevate them to the middle of the pack in the rankings.

The first is the play of Wilson, who won her fourth regular-season MVP and second Finals MVP. During the playoffs, she averaged 26.8 PPG, 10.0 RPG, 3.3 assists and 2.5 blocks. Her postseason performance was even greater than in the Regular-season. She also hit the most crucial shot of the Finals: the game winner with less than a second left in Game 3 to give the Aces a 90-88 victory.

The Aces also got a terrific postseason from guards Jackie Young (20.4 PPG, 5.5 APG) and Chelsea Gray (11.2 PPG, 7.3 APG).

The Aces' 17-game winning streak (counting Game 1 of the playoffs) is the second longest in WNBA history. And coach Becky Hammon led the Aces to a third championship in four years despite having to replace a key player (guard Kelsey Plum) from the first two title teams. The Aces are the league's ultimate example that it's not how you start, it's how you finish.

16. 2018 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-2

Defeated the Washington Mystics 3-0 in Finals

History repeated itself with the Storm. They had back-to-back No. 1 picks in Jackson and Bird in 2001 and 2002, which led to two titles. Seattle again got consecutive No. 1s in 2015 and 2016 with Loyd and Stewart, which also led to two titles. This 2018 championship in a lot of ways was won in the semifinals, when the Storm held off Phoenix in an epic Game 5 in which Bird took over in the fourth quarter. In the finals, Seattle wasn't going to be denied and swept the Mystics. And the Storm looked to be a strong threat to become the first repeat champion since the Sparks in 2001-02. But an Achilles injury kept Stewart out in 2019. When she returned in 2020, the Storm picked up where they had left off in 2018.

17. 2010 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 28-6, 7-0

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

The 2010 Storm were six games better than any team in the WNBA; no other team in the Western Conference even had a winning record. Jackson won her third MVP award, and she and Bird got to celebrate their second WNBA championship together. Bird, Swin Cash and Svetlana Abrosimova, who had won an NCAA title together at UConn in 2000, all played for this Storm team. Seattle didn't lose at home in 2010, which ended up being Jackson's last full season in the WNBA, as injuries forced her out of the league after 2012.

18. 2005 Sacramento Monarchs

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-9, 7-1

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-1 in Finals

After losing in the conference finals three of the previous four years, the Monarchs won in 2005.

At age 29, Yolanda Griffith entered the WNBA in 1999 from the ABL and was her new league's MVP that year, a perfect target for point guard Ticha Penicheiro.

Griffith also won Finals MVP, and it was a career-best year for DeMya Walker, who led the Monarchs in scoring in the Regular-season and made an All-Star appearance. This was also the first of Rebekkah Brunson's five WNBA titles; her other four came with Minnesota.

19. 2002 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-7, 6-0

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-0 in Finals

The Sparks' repeat championship seemed more predictable than extraordinary at the time, coming after Houston had won four in a row. But it took two decades for another franchise to go back-to-back, with the Aces doing it in 2022-2023. That makes Los Angeles' achievement stand out more now. There isn't much to separate this Sparks team from the 2001 Sparks, who had a little better regular-season record (28-4 in 2001 to 25-7 in 2002). The standout players were the same except for Nikki Teasley, a rookie in 2002 who hit the championship-clinching 3-pointer in Game 2 of the Finals.

20. 2026 Golden State Valkyries

Regular-season and playoff records: 32-12, 9-4

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 4-3 in Finals

Much has been made of the Valkyries being the first champions without any All-WNBA selections in the season they won the title. They also are the first team since the 2013 Minnesota Lynx to not have a current or former season MVP on the roster at the time of their championship.

This largely reflects the Valkyries' focus on defense: The All-WNBA first and second teams are generally tilted toward big offensive stats. So a lot of credit must go to Golden State's team chemistry and an outstanding coaching job by Natalie Nakase and her staff.

In the playoffs, the Valkyries beat teams with some of the top offensive players in the league: Dallas' Paige Bueckers and Arike Ogunbowale, Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray, and Atlanta's Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray.

As mentioned, the Valkyries are one of five WNBA champions who averaged fewer points in the Finals than their opponent (67.4 PPG to Atlanta's 71.4); the others are Las Vegas (2022), Los Angeles (2016), and Detroit twice (2006, 2003). But the Dream's Finals scoring average was still 20 points lower than their regular-season average, plus Golden State held Atlanta under 65 points in all four of its victories.

It was very impressive, and as time passes, the Valkyries' performance might move up even more in historical regard.

21. 2006 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-3

Defeated the Sacramento Monarchs 3-2 in Finals

A big key for this team was the 2005 midseason trade that brought Katie Smith to the Shock. She fit in well with Cash, Cheryl Ford, Deanna Nolan and Ruth Riley, who were all on Detroit's 2003 championship squad.

Nolan, a native of nearby Flint, Michigan, was Finals MVP as the Shock prevented Sacramento's attempt at a repeat. In the decisive Game 5, won 80-75 by Detroit, Nolan played all 40 minutes and scored 24 points.

22. 2012 Indiana Fever

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-1 in Finals

When Indiana lost its playoff opener 75-66 at home to Atlanta, there was no reason to think anything magical was in the works. Yet the Fever won the next two games and the series. The Fever also lost their opener in the East finals to Connecticut, but won 2-1 again.

Next up: A Lynx team that had the best record in the league that year. The Fever and Lynx split the first two games of the Finals. But in Game 3, the Lynx -- who led the league in offensive rating -- were held to a season-low 59 points.

Indiana had been up 2-1 in the 2009 Finals yet lost the series to Phoenix. But in 2012, franchise legend Tamika Catchings got her long-awaited title as the Fever won Game 4 at home.

23. 2007 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-2

Defeated the Detroit Shock 3-2 in Finals

Three years after winning her third title at UConn, Taurasi won her first WNBA championship. Phoenix's winning formula was coach Paul Westhead's run-and-gun offense, which was first in the league. Defense was not as much a priority; the Mercury were next-to-last in defensive rating. But it worked, with Taurasi, Taylor, Cappie Pondexter and Tangela Smith all averaging double digits in scoring.

The Finals matchup with defending champion Detroit got chippy, with Phoenix surviving a physical Game 4 in a 77-76 win. Then the Mercury became the first WNBA team to win a championship on the road, taking Game 5 108-92 at Detroit behind 30 points from Taylor -- who went 18 of 18 from the free throw line -- and 26 points and 10 assists from Finals MVP Pondexter.

24. 2004 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 20-14, 6-2

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 2-1 in Finals

This was Seattle's first trip to the WNBA Finals. And this was the last year that the Finals was a best-of-three series. The Storm were on the ropes after a 68-64 opening loss at Connecticut. But they pulled out a 67-65 nail-biter in Game 2 at Seattle, led by Betty Lennox's 27 points. In Game 3, with KeyArena packed with Storm fans wielding thunder sticks, Lennox had 23 points and earned Finals MVP honors as Seattle clinched the title 74-60.

25. 2015 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-3

Defeated the Indiana Fever 3-2 in Finals

Of the Lynx's four title teams, this was the only one with double-digit losses, as Augustus and Whalen both dealt with injuries. But big-time help came via two trades in July: first for guard Renee Montgomery and then for center Sylvia Fowles, who had sat out the season to that point to force a trade from Chicago.

Moore, the 2014 MVP, was again brilliant in 2015, leading the Lynx in scoring in the Regular-season (20.6 PPG) and the postseason (23.4). She hit a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to win Game 3 of the Finals vs. Indiana 80-77. The Fever won Game 4, but Fowles cemented her Finals MVP award with 20 points and 11 rebounds in a Game 5 victory.

26. 2009 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-4

Defeated the Indiana Fever 3-2 in Finals

This was a good team led by a great player in Taurasi, who won her only regular-season MVP award in 2009. Like the 2007 champions, the Mercury focused on outscoring foes: Phoenix was first in offensive rating and last in defensive rating. Five players averaged in double figures, led by Taurasi's 20.4 PPG and Pondexter's 19.1.

The first game of the 2009 Finals was amazing: a 120-116 Mercury victory over Indiana. But the Fever took the next two games and had a chance to close out the series at home. Phoenix's defense showed up for Game 4, holding the Fever to a series-low 77 points. In Game 5, Taurasi and Pondexter combined for 50 points to win their last game as Phoenix teammates. Pondexter requested and got a trade to New York the next year.

27. 2021 Chicago Sky
Regular-season and playoff records: 16-16, 8-2

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 3-1 in Finals

With longtime Sparks star Candace Parker coming to her hometown of Chicago as a free agent, there were big expectations for the 2021 Sky. Chicago went .500 in the Regular-season, the worst record of any championship team. But all the pieces were there -- including point guard Courtney Vandersloot and guard/forward Kahleah Copper -- to win a title.

The No. 6 seed, the Sky beat Dallas in the first round and Minnesota in the second. Then they went against No. 1 seed Connecticut in the semifinals. A double-overtime win in the first game of the series was pivotal, and Chicago won 3-1. In the Finals, the Sky won 3-1 over Phoenix, with Parker celebrating with family as the franchise won its first title.

28. 1997 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 18-10, 2-0

Defeated the New York Liberty in championship game

This is where it all started, with the Comets winning the inaugural championship of the WNBA, which launched with eight teams. Cooper at age 34 was the best player in the new league, averaging 22.2 points and being named MVP. They played just single-game semifinals and finals in the first year, and Cooper scored 31 and 25 points in those victories. Thompson, who had been the top pick in the college draft, averaged 13.2 points and Brazil's Arcain 10.9. Swoopes gave birth to a son on June 25, just after the WNBA season had started. She played her first game on Aug. 7, and appeared in nine regular-season and two playoff games.

29. 2008 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-2

Defeated the San Antonio Silver Stars 3-0 in Finals

By the time the Stars met the Shock in the WNBA Finals, Detroit was the better team. Five Shock players averaged in double figures in the Regular-season, led by Nolan and Smith. A late-season trade brought McWilliams-Franklin to Detroit, and she averaged 12.9 points and 7.8 rebounds in the playoffs. Smith won Finals MVP honors as the Shock won their third WNBA title in six years.

Unfortunately, the franchise was nearing its end in Detroit. The Shock played just one more season in the Motor City before moving to Tulsa in 2010.

30. 2003 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-9, 6-2

Defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 2-1 in Finals

The Shock went from worst in 2002 (9-23) to first in 2003, ending the Sparks' attempt to three-peat. Former Pistons player Bill Laimbeer took over as Shock coach during the 2002 season and totally changed the team's culture. He drafted Cheryl Ford at No. 3 in 2003; she averaged a double-double (10.8 PPG, 10.4 RPG) and was Rookie of the Year. Cash, who had been the No. 2 pick in 2002, led the Shock with 16.6 points in the Regular-season and 16.3 in the playoffs.

Detroit lost the Finals opener to Los Angeles, but survived Game 2, winning 62-61. In front of a huge crowd at The Palace at Auburn Hills, the Shock took the title in Game 3 in an 83-78 win, led by 27 points from Finals MVP Ruth Riley and Cash's near triple-double (13 points, 12 rebounds, 9 assists).

"I think our team really embodied the city of Detroit," Cash said.

stories.headline: Noni Madueke: Alexis Mac Allister tried to 'bait me' into red card
stories.summary: Noni Madueke has said that Alexis Mac Allister tried to "bait" him into getting a red card during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.
stories.body:
Noni Madueke has said that Alexis Mac Allister tried to "bait" him into getting a red card during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.

The Argentine midfielder went to ground while he and Madueke were face-to-face in the 79th minute of the match and Madueke was not punished.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Madueke said that he didn't think there was "anything" in the incident.

"To be honest, I don't think it's anything -- a yellow card or a red card. The referee didn't think that, VAR [Video Assistant Referee] didn't think that, so we all agreed there," the Arsenal forward said.

"It's a natural movement and he's obviously clever, he tried to bait me into getting a red card there but obviously no. In my head, I was thinking it's possible [to be sent off] with VAR, with whoever interprets it -- I don't know what they're thinking... But thankfully it wasn't."

The Gunners claimed victory at Anfield for the first time in 14 years as Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game.

Mac Allister was criticised by Jamie Carragher for his role in the incident between himself and Madueke.

On Sky Sports, Carragher said: "I am delighted [Madueke] never got sent off there. "We have got to be strong in calling people out and saying 'this is embarrassing.'

"It has got to stop, it's ridiculous. I can't stand it.

"If someone puts their head back then butts, of course it's a red card. But this stuff about a head-to-head, and if someone touches the other one goes down and it's a red card?

- Arsenal hold on for a big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from

- Declan Rice tops Premier League assist chart - without set-pieces

- Dominik Szoboszlai asks if Liverpool expected to 'dive' to win penalty

"As a game, as football, people in the Premier League and supporters [must] call your own people out for it.

"I am a Liverpool fan and that's a joke from Mac Allister. It's got to stop.

"People are trying to game the system because they know that they can. Red cards are being given for it.

"Whether it's from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers -- stop getting red cards for this."

stories.headline: Monday's fantasy hoops adds, NBA bets to make: How to bet Tatum, Jokic and more
stories.summary: Andre Snellings breaks down Monday's full NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
stories.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Monday
The NBA will not have any games on Tuesday due to Election Day, so every team in the league will play on Monday. That's right, today features 15 games and 30 teams in action. Three of those games feature two teams above .500 facing off, starting in Cleveland where the 4-2 Cavaliers host the 4-2 Oklahoma City Thunder. Both teams have contending aspirations and are off to good starts, but the Thunder have been beset by early season injury that they are battling to overcome.

The 6-1 Houston Rockets will host the 5-1 Boston Celtics in another Ime Udoka classic, where the head coach of the Rockets faces his former team. This game also gives us a matchup between two of the elite big perimeter forwards in the league in Kevin Durant versus Jayson Tatum.

Finally, in Denver, the 3-2 Nuggets host the 4-1 Portland Trail Blazers. The Trail Blazers are off to a surprisingly hot start, including a perfect 3-0 road record that will be tested in the Mile High City.

These, and many other storylines will be on display in tonight's jam-packed slate. As we do, let's dig deeper into the matchups to identify some fantasy streamer options and betting angles of interest.

Fantasy stream team
Players available in at least 50% of leagues

Anthony Black, PG/SG, Orlando Magic (Rostered in 48.0% of ESPN leagues)
Black has started three straight games with teammates Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs sidelined, and in his last two has averaged 20.0 PPG, 7.0 RPG and 6.5 APG in 32.0 MPG.

Jeremiah Fears, SG/PG, New Orleans Pelicans (46.6%)
Fears has been scorching from the field and taking on a larger role as a playmaker in his last couple of outings, putting up 21.0 PPG, 10.0 APG and 6.5 RPG in those two games.

Dillon Brooks, SF/SG, Phoenix Suns (32.3%)

stories.headline: Who's No. 1? Our definitive ranking of the NHL's new Hometown Remix jerseys
stories.summary: Here is our ranking of the 32 NHL Hometown Remix jerseys for the 2026-27 season.
stories.body:
The NHL Hometown Remix jerseys are here, and some of them are spectacular.

And some of them aren't.

When Fanatics became the NHL's official on-ice uniform outfitter in the 2024-25 season, it was expected to take a couple of seasons before attempting its first "all 32 teams" alternate jersey project, like the Reverse Retro jerseys Adidas created for the NHL in 2020 and 2022.

"It was always envisioned with 'How do we do something different than what Adidas did with Reverse Retro 1.0 and 2.0?'" said Brian Jennings, NHL chief branding officer and senior executive vice president.

Enter NHL Hometown Remix jerseys, which officially launched Monday morning after weeks of tantalizing leaks.

The concept was simple: Have teams create distinct new looks that would theoretically tie back to the places they play and the fans for whom they play.

"When Hometown Remix came in and we started those conversations, I was like, 'OK, there's something here in this hyperlocal thing.' The part that got me really excited was the buy-in from the clubs," Jennings said.

Some teams seemed to really understand the assignment, and others sort of faked their way through it.

Here is our ranking of the 32 NHL Hometown Remix jerseys for the 2026-27 season, which (for now) is expected to be the only season in which they're worn.

We've reviewed the jerseys in person at Fanatics and have seen what they look like with a full uniform and on the ice. Our ranking is based on how good they look, how innovative they are and how well they tie in with the mission of the Hometown Remix jerseys.

Let's start with what we consider to be the best.

No. 1: Pittsburgh Penguins

Andy Warhol, then Andrew Warhola Jr., was born in Pittsburgh in 1928, nearly 40 years before the Penguins entered the NHL. His ties to the city -- home to The Andy Warhol Museum -- are part of a larger connection between the pop art movement and Pittsburgh, carried on by locals such as Burton Morris.

If the primary ethos of the Hometown Remix project is to connect the jersey to the city, then Pittsburgh gets enormous credit for doing it without relying on, say, architecture or weather phenomena. It doesn't mine franchise history for an obscure look from which to draw; it's reimagining the team's primary logo for the better part of 55 years, although it nods to previous team color schemes, too.

But that's only half the mission for the Hometown Remix jersey project. The other is "does this look good?"

We'd argue it looks the best.

Lost in the Microsoft Paint leak mockups was the offset outline around the Penguin, giving it a sense of motion while also being slightly disorienting. The dotted yellow background of the logo is like if Roy Lichtenstein were commissioned to create a Stadium Series jersey. It's the epitome of pop art: Something familiar, from the Igloo tribute on the shoulder to the numbers on the back, reinterpreted in a way that uses that nostalgia to push in a bold new direction.

There are probably very good, potentially litigious reasons they couldn't go full Warhol here -- imagine a jersey with the same four logos on the front done in the style of Warhol's Campbell's soup can? However, we did love the nod to his art on the hem as the word "Pittsburgh" is repeated several times in several colors to represent the city's different boroughs.

Both jersey rankings and art are inherently subjective. From our perspective, nothing in this batch of new sweaters married concept and execution better than the Penguins did. These are the best.

No. 2: Anaheim Ducks

Finally answering the question: What if Anaheim had entered the NHL leaning all the way in to its namesake and dressed like Gordon Bombay's Mighty Ducks?

Fanatics has a bunch of stuff in its media materials about the fresh green parks and golden sunsets of Orange County. But this is Charlie Conway. This is Marguerite Moreau. This is the Flying V and "fly together." This is "The Mighty Ducks," through and through. It's a jersey that would have 100% turned up in a SoCal hip-hop video voted No. 1 on "TRL" in 1998.

It also made us wonder whether New Orleans should get an NHL expansion team, because this jersey also looks a few shades (and bead necklaces) away from being Mardi Gras-ready.

No. 3: Florida Panthers

The Panthers had the best Reverse Retro 2.0 jersey back in 2022 when they finally made their stick-and-palm secondary logo their primary crest, ending a 30-year run of sweaters that did everything but evoke South Florida.

Well, there's no mistaking South Florida this time, folks! The Panthers run back that awesome logo augmented by a sunrise -- the team plays in Sunrise, for locality's sake -- whose colors are used throughout the jersey. That includes the most distinct and bold primary color ever seen on an NHL jersey.

They call it "coral." Everyone else will call it pink. Whatever you call it, the Panthers took a swing few have taken in a pro sports jersey -- although it should be noted that the MLS' Inter Miami walked so Florida could skate in "coral."

An undeniable facet of this jersey's success is that the right group of players is wearing them. Few teams are as in-your-face as the Panthers, literally and figuratively. The juxtaposition between some of the NHL's most unrelentingly nasty and physical players and a jersey that looks like a beach cocktail is intoxicating. Radko Gudas is going to throw one of these jerseys, folks. Let that soak in.

No. 4: Nashville Predators

Outside of some guitar strings on the numbers and piano keys in the collar, the Predators have never really leaned in to the honky-tonk of it all in Nashville. Creating a jersey that looks like country music stage wear -- from the flourishes on the shoulders to the filigree in the crest -- is such an obvious winner in retrospect. It's sort of amazing it took this long.

While many of us will be enthralled by a team that looks ready to play a cover of "I Walk the Line" at Tootsies, Predators fans are no doubt happy to see the team return to a sharp navy base for the first time in around 15 years. It's a valentine to the Broadway music bars near the arena, a nod to some great Predators uniforms of the past and just a stellar hockey jersey.

No. 5: Montreal Canadiens

It's hard to pull off an innovative and compelling white jersey, as evidenced by the Hometown Remix program having produced only four of them. The Canadiens' sweater is easily the best of that bunch and a contender for best overall, given how it looks and the story it tells.

On the sleeves: white pine, fleur-de-lys, rose, thistle and clover. The five symbols on the flag of Montreal, whose red and white colorway inform the rest of this design. The side panels are meant to evoke the eponymous Mount Royal. The number system is inspired by Old Montreal. The crest has texturing designed to honor the stonework around the city.

Montreal's specialty jerseys have typically dipped back into the franchise's history for inspiration -- remember the "barber pole" sweaters from its centennial celebration? Well, these keep the general template of a Canadiens jersey. There's a real audacity to the design, given the jerseys that have come before them. These sweaters are going to look magnifique on the ice and are a deeply detailed love letter to the city that loves its Habs endlessly.

No. 6: Washington Capitals

Amanda Tischler, the Capitals' senior vice president of marketing, told ESPN it was a happy accident that their Hometown Remix jersey runs back the Capitol dome logo the team wore when Alex Ovechkin entered the NHL, just as the Great 8 is in his final season in the league.

There are few other Hometown Remix jerseys that seem like they should have been a team's primary jersey sometime in the past. We're so accustomed to "Rock the Red" that we forget their jerseys didn't even have that color for about a dozen years in the 1990s and early aughts.

Along with the dome, the other local connection is the marble texturing of the sleeves and shoulder yoke. We think it's pretty innovative, but it's also understandable that some might see it as one gimmick too many. One person's "Wow, it looks like a D.C. monument!" is another person's "Why do the shoulders look dirty?"

No. 7: Detroit Red Wings

As you'll see later in this ranking, challenging an Original Six team to remix a nearly century-old look isn't easy. That especially goes for the Red Wings, whose Winged Wheel is one of the most iconic looks in sports. They're not going to suddenly bust out a purple jersey with an octopus maw on the front. They're just not.

The cephalopod is referenced on the hem of the jersey, but the rest of the sweater is dedicated to two dogmas: that the Red Wings' jerseys can't be improved on and that even in these dark times for the franchise, Detroit is still "Hockeytown." They've had words atop their logo before (such as on their 2014 Winter Classic sweaters) but had never had "Hockeytown" so front and center. These rock.

No. 8: Toronto Maple Leafs

There are a few jerseys in this ranking that could have finished much higher were it not for one or two missteps in design.

The good for Toronto: The remixing of its primary logo, with its eye-catching silhouette and intricate texturing that's carried over to the sleeves and the numbers. We also love that the various "Leafs" that have appeared on their jerseys are represented on the hem. The wordmark is large, making the whole front of the jersey a bit grandiose in keeping with the Centre of the Hockey Universe™.

The not as good for Toronto: Those white stripes harsh the vibe, don't they? Obviously, white sleeve striping on Leafs sweaters tracks back to 1927. But here, they just don't seem like a piece with the rest of the fit. They throw the whole thing off balance, like a confused spouse throwing multicolored carnations into a bouquet of a dozen roses.

No. 9: Carolina Hurricanes

Hot take: The Hurricanes need a new logo. This is a hard argument to make when they just lifted the Stanley Cup while wearing their swirly toilet flush logo, but the sentiment remains.

Whether this collegiate rendering of their mascot, Stormy, could ever become their primary mark is debatable, but it's a step up. The problem here is that the logo is featured on a drab gray sweater that's inferior to the team's red and black looks.

One thing we do like here: All the nods to the "City of Oaks," including oak leaves debossed on the sleeves.

No. 10: Vegas Golden Knights

Gambling references? On the uniform of a team based in Las Vegas? Is that even allowed?!

The Golden Knights finally lean in to casino iconography with felt table green on the shoulders, a roulette wheel pattern on the sleeves and socks, a typeface inspired by playing cards, and different card suits found around the jersey. Plus, there's an embossed script "Vegas" on the arms. It's a distinct look for the Knights that finally connects with everything around them on The Strip -- although it would have been fun to see the primary logo rendered in a winning slot machine combo. Maybe next time.

No. 11: Minnesota Wild

We went back and forth on this one. Black jerseys are beyond cliché. The Wild have traded in one of the NHL's most distinct color schemes for something that screams "recently relocated AHL franchise."

But this jersey improves mightily upon further inspection. Their primary logo has never looked better. The sleeves have a debossed Ursa Major and Ursa Minor, and the numbers have stars to evoke the Twin Cities. As an ode to cold Minnesota nights on the pond -- and the mysteries of space -- we're here for it.

No. 12: Dallas Stars

This is essentially a neon electrified version of the Stars' current road jerseys, with much bolder striping. The texture on the crest is supposed to be inspired by the city's skyline at night. Dallas could have gone a hundred ways with these jerseys, but the path it chose produced a stark on-ice look, if not exactly an innovative or city-specific one. But a must-own for fans of Monster Energy drink, one assumes.

No. 13: Columbus Blue Jackets

These would have gone so much harder had the Blue Jackets not worn their cannon as the primary crest of their 2025 NHL Stadium Series jerseys. These are still solid, and it's the first time the Blue Jackets have used gray as the base color for one of their jerseys. Maybe the best thing about these are the large stripes on the sleeves. The arching on them is in reference to Columbus being the "Arch City." They also threw a little "5th Line" graphic on the hem for the fans.

No. 14: Los Angeles Kings

The Kings are fighting history in their Hometown Remix look, which takes all their previous looks and puts them in a blender set to "streetwear."

The Kings did similar things to better success in their Reverse Retro 1.0 and 2.0 sweaters. These are still really solid and have some nice innovations -- the "Hollywood-inspired serif font" used for Los Angeles in the logo is sublime. But the palm leaves embossed on the sleeves are giving barbed-wire bicep tattoo from the 1990s.

No. 15: Tampa Bay Lightning

When the Tampa Bay Lightning released their Stadium Series jerseys last season, the hockey world had one question: "Hey, why wasn't that awesome Gasparilla-adjacent pirate skull logo on the shoulder the primary logo instead?" Maybe because it was already on deck for the Hometown Remix.

The David Bowie-esque lightning bolt on the skull -- and the missing tooth they gave it in this incarnation -- makes this one of the better alternate logos in hockey. But again, what could have been: Imagine how sweet these jerseys would be with a blue base and a black logo, rather than becoming the sixth variation of a black-based jersey in team history. (Don't they know black absorbs more heat and they play in Florida?)

No. 16: Seattle Kraken

Speaking of secondary logos that maybe deserve more prominence, the Kraken take their "Space Needle-as-anchor" logo from the shoulder to the front of the sweater, and it looks iconic. There are a lot of other local details on these, from a nod to Mt. Rainier on the sleeves to rhododendrons on the hem.

As Fanatics notes: "The new name and number system features custom nautical-inspired typography with meticulous scrimshaw embroidery, while the shoulder patch also brings scrimshaw detailing to the fore." One can never have enough scrimshaw.

No. 17: New York Islanders

The circle is complete. The fisherman jersey was one of the most widely mocked in NHL history, from the Islanders being called the "fish sticks" to those who felt its color scheme was reminiscent of toothpaste stripes. After being resurrected for Reverse Retro 2.0, the fisherman is back with something closer to the original colorway from the 1990s. The logo has never looked better, and the entire jersey system looks great on the ice. Consider yourself redeemed, Mr. Fishsticks.

No. 18: Ottawa Senators

This feels like a Pokémon evolution of their current jersey, like Ottawa got to a certain experience level and everything became "metallic gold lurex." The bilingual shoulder patches are a nice touch. The geometric striping on the sleeves is giving both Ottawa gothic architecture and Doctor Doom spellcasting runes.

No. 19: San Jose Sharks

The teeth. It's all about the teeth. The look is clean. The logo has a youthful vibe to it that fits the surging rebuild in San Jose, led by star Macklin Celebrini. But we can't get past the teeth on the sleeves, which is giving a video game-like "create-a-jersey" rather than an ascendant Stanley Cup contender.

OK, if we're being honest: It's not the teeth, it's the gums. So many gums. There's a reason one of the greatest summer blockbusters of all time wasn't called "Gums." Less gums, more jaws, please.

No. 20: Edmonton Oilers

Having a jersey that looks like it was dipped into a barrel of crude oil is either the greatest evocation of the Edmontonian aesthetic or a flimsy excuse to join the black jersey parade. Frankly, we were going to rank these a bit lower, but then someone mentioned they're reminiscent of the all-time classic World Cup of Hockey Team North America jerseys from 2016, which Connor McDavid also wore.

No. 21: Buffalo Sabres

We can already hear people grabbing their pitchforks over this mashup of iconic Buffalo Sabres looks being ranked so low. But just like how a DJ can cut together two classic songs to make a mediocre one, the Sabres' gorgeous blue sweaters mixed with "goat head" crests aren't in harmony.

This is the same issue we had back in 2022 when the Sabres put the "goat head" on a white-and-blue jersey for Reverse Retro 2.0. We actually ranked them 23rd overall in that tabulation, writing: "The 'goat head' logo loses its magic when stripped away from the red, black and silver color scheme that evoked images of Dominik Hasek saves and Miroslav Satan goals." The sentiment still stands.

No. 22: Calgary Flames

This one gets an "A" for concept alone: an entire jersey commemorating Calgary's final season in the Saddledome. That includes debossing on the sleeves to represent the arena's windows and the roofline being represented on the hem of the sweater. Unfortunately, using the texture of the arena ceiling on the "Flaming C" logo leaves it looking like an ode to breakfast waffles.

No. 23: New Jersey Devils

Is Lou Lamoriello still running this team? After breaking the template with the "Jersey" jerseys, which are now retired, the Devils retreated to what's essentially a black base version of their 2024 Stadium Series jersey. Not a bad-looking jersey at all, but it still feels like a missed opportunity given the team's name -- not to mention there's little "Hometown" in this remix.

No. 24: Winnipeg Jets

The Jets went in an interesting direction with their Hometown Remix sweaters: skyward. These jerseys are inspired by the Aurora Borealis, which can be seen in Winnipeg during the fall and winter. The jet on the crest is supposed to look like it has been lit by the Northern Lights, and the names and numbers are supposed to seem like they're glowing.

Neat idea, even if they're giving "what if we did tie-dye our Connor Hellebuyck jersey we're never wearing again?" energy.

No. 25: Philadelphia Flyers

We want to be kind to these jerseys, because the amount of detail in them is remarkable. The Flyers went with the Liberty Bell as inspiration, drawing everything from the spacing of the jersey's stripes to using the actual inscription on the bell on the sleeves to having a "crack" in their numbers system. But the Flyers are, and ever shall be, the orange and black. Making gray the primary color of a Flyers jersey -- while novel! -- just doesn't fit the motif.

No. 26: Utah Mammoth

The primary logo is Utah's secondary logo: a "U" with a tusk swooping through it. These are fine. What did you think you were getting? Snow kachina?

No. 27: Colorado Avalanche

The Avalanche topped our Reverse Retro 1.0 ranking with their Quebec Nordiques throwback. Their follow-up was less iconic, but a nice-looking sweater that incorporated the state flag. Their Hometown Remix sweater also uses that logo in a "frosted, glistening" ode to the Rocky Mountains. Perfect if you're cosplaying Elsa from "Frozen" as Cale Makar, less so as a specialty jersey.

No. 28: Boston Bruins

The Bruins have had a lot of different jerseys in the past 100 years, including nine different outdoor game looks. At some point, the wells of inspiration run a little dry. So for the Hometown Remix campaign, the team went with, "Hey, Boston sure does have a lot of colleges, huh?" Get one at your local campus bookstore.

No. 29: St. Louis Blues

The Blues have done this logo and look before as a third jersey and they were awesome in a way this one is not. But the real flaws in this Blues Remix sweater are all the forced references to the Mississippi River, from the ripples on the arms to the little wavey lines around the crest. Fanatics said: "Inspired by the dark waters of the Mississippi, black makes a striking appearance as the primary jersey color." OK then.

No. 30: Vancouver Canucks

This is, like, the third or fourth jersey to celebrate "the city after dark" and by far the most ordinary, even with the city skyline on the sleeves. The crest features "a stealth-mode orca in deep blues with shining silver eyes," which sure sounds better than it looks.

No. 31: New York Rangers

The Rangers' specialty jerseys either have some diagonal wordmark or one of two logos they've used since the 1990s. For their Hometown Remix jersey, they have some diagonal wordmark AND one of two logos they've used since the 1990s, in this case the famed Liberty Head.

No. 32: Chicago Blackhawks

Finally, here's an unfortunate manufacturing error in which a Chicago Blackhawks logo was mistakenly stitched onto a Dallas Stars jersey!

Wait, hold on, we're now being told this is the Blackhawks' Hometown Remix jersey.

For the first time, the team will wear a green jersey during games, as their green St. Patrick's Day jerseys were only worn in warmups back in the day. The Chicago flag is represented with four debossed stars on the sleeves to connect it to the city.

Why are the Blackhawks ranked last? Because they play in Chicago, a city with an endless amount of aesthetics and iconography that could make for an instant classic jersey.

This program is supposed to give teams the chance to highlight their locations or bond themselves to something locally iconic. Even if you wanted to make the case that these jerseys celebrate making the river green for St. Patrick's Day, it's still more about a random holiday than the city and its people. Wrestler CM Punk has a deeper connection to Chicago with his wrestling trunks. Use the flag. Use The Bean. Put a picture of Cousin from "The Bear" serving an Italian Beef Sandwich. Have a cow kicking over a lantern on the hem. Anything!

It's a missed opportunity and hopefully a lesson learned for whatever the next jersey program ends up being in the NHL.

stories.headline: Trial begins for Guardians' Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz in pitch-rigging case
stories.summary: The trial of two major league baseball pitchers accused of rigging pitches in a betting scheme begins Monday in federal court in Brooklyn.
stories.body:
The trial of two major league baseball pitchers accused of rigging pitches in a betting scheme begins Monday with jury selection in federal court in New York.

Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase de la Cruz and Luis Leandro Ortiz Ribera are charged with conspiracy to commit wire and honest services fraud, sports bribery and money laundering.

Co-defendants Robinson Vásquez Germosen and Luis Arismendy Paca Méndez are accused of sharing inside information from Clase, 28, with other bettors and using that information to wager on what federal prosecutors say were predetermined pitches.

Paca Méndez, who prosecutors allege lived with Clase at his house in Ohio during part of the scheme, will not take part in the trial in Brooklyn after being extradited from the Dominican Republic to the U.S. on Oct. 19, according to a spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York.

Guardians front office personnel, including general manager Mike Chernoff, as well as coaches and catchers who worked with Clase and Ortiz are among the potential witnesses, along with officials from Major League Baseball and DraftKings.

The government alleges that Clase, one of the best closers in baseball, rigged at least 18 pitches in 17 games from May 19, 2023, to May 28, 2025, often by intentionally throwing balls or by tipping off bettors that he would throw an off-speed pitch. Prosecutors say he shared information about the planned result or the velocity of the pitches with bettors, including Vásquez and Méndez, using code words like "rooster" and "chicken," sometimes in exchange for "bribe and kickback payments."

The bettors allegedly placed more than 100 wagers and won at least $400,000 on Clase's pitches. In a hearing Friday, attorneys disclosed that the bets were placed with DraftKings, FanDuel and ESPN BET.

Clase's attorneys have argued that his pitches were part of normal baseball strategy. "At trial, the jury will be tasked with deciding if certain ... pitches were thrown for legitimate, baseball-strategy reasons or in furtherance of a scheme to defraud betting companies," his attorneys wrote in a September filing. "In isolation, any single pitch in the dirt can be painted as nefarious."

In a January filing, Clase's attorneys said that he did not participate in a conspiracy and instead had communicated with his associates about gambling on rooster fighting in the Dominican Republic, where it is legal. They added that Clase and Ortiz moved money to their home country to buy and care for livestock, including a horse.

During the hearing Friday, prosecutors said they recently learned that Clase owes the IRS about $500,000, which they argued showed motive for the alleged bribes. Clase's attorneys denied in court that their client had a financial motive. The judge ruled the information inadmissible for trial.

ESPN obtained records of a federal tax lien listed under Clase's name in Maricopa County, Arizona, for $588,919.60 in back taxes from 2022 to 2024. The lien was issued in May 2026.

Ortiz, 27, is accused of manipulating two pitches in two Guardians games in June 2025, according to the indictment. Prosecutors say Ortiz was in debt to a company that advances money to professional athletes against their future earnings.

In a September filing, Ortiz's attorneys said that he never communicated with the bettors: "Not once. Not by text, not by phone, not in person."

"The government's case against Luis Leandro Ortiz Ribera is remarkably thin," Ortiz's attorneys wrote. "It consists, in essence, of the anticipated testimony of two cooperating bettors ... and a handful of wagers that [they] and two of their relatives placed on two pitches Mr. Ortiz threw."

The alleged scheme came to light after sportsbooks flagged unusual betting interest on Ortiz's first pitch in the bottom of the second inning on June 15, 2025, against the Seattle Mariners, and his first pitch in the top of the third inning against the St. Louis Cardinals on June 27, 2025.

In a court filing, the government said the size of the bets on the two Ortiz pitches was up to "136 times greater" than the average wager placed by the bettors allegedly involved. MLB has since asked sportsbooks to place a maximum $200 betting limit on wagers on individual pitches and to prohibit such bets from being included in parlays.

MLB placed Ortiz and Clase on non-disciplinary paid leave in July 2025. The two were indicted four months later.

Clase earned more than $13 million over a seven-year major league career, and he was scheduled to make $6.4 million in 2026. Ortiz's salary in 2025 was $782,600.

Attorneys for Clase, Ortiz and Paca Méndez did not respond to requests for comment from ESPN. A U.S. Attorney's Office spokesperson declined ESPN's request for comment about the trial.

Vásquez's attorney, Todd Spodek, told ESPN that his client is innocent.

"People forget that an indictment is just the government's side of the story," he said. "Mr. Vásquez is innocent, and we're confident that the evidence will support this."

In court documents filed days before the trial, the prosecution and defense sparred over the translation from Spanish to English of text messages, videos and voice memos that will be used as evidence. A Spanish-language interpreter will participate in the proceedings.

Judge Kiyo A. Matsumoto will oversee the trial, which the government estimates will last three weeks.

The wire fraud, honest services and money laundering charges carry maximum prison sentences of 20 years, while the sports bribery charge has a five-year maximum prison sentence, according to the Department of Justice.

The case is one of five federal sports gambling cases involving alleged performance manipulation by professional or college athletes over the past three years -- and the first to go to trial.

ESPN reporter Michael Rothstein and ESPN researcher John Mastroberardino contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot
stories.summary: Inter Miami CF beat the New England Revolution 2-1 on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts, with Lionel Messi once again providing the magic touch, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.
stories.body:
Inter Miami CF beat the New England Revolution 2-1 on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts, with Lionel Messi once again providing the magic touch, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The win also helped Miami leapfrog the Revs into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

"It makes me very happy for the players and for the club, we are on the side of contributing things," Miami manager Cristian González said after the game. "We are at a club that is in continuous growth, I have players committed to us. We needed to win and we challenged ourselves on what kind of team we wanted to be."

The Revolution edged out Inter Miami in the first half, registering six total shots, five corner kicks and generating an expected goals of .75, but the match went to the break tied 0-0.

Dániel Gazdag then opened up the scoring in the initial minutes of the second half, connecting with Ilay Feingold inside the box before finding the back of the net.

Miami found a way to respond to Gazdag's strike with a goal from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- in the 69th minute. González then bolstered Inter Miami's attack after drawing level, substituting in Luis Suárez, who had started Miami's last 25 games.

"We knew we were going up against a rival that tries to seek out duels where they defend high, so the possibility of changes was to have depth, look for the spaces, and the one-on-one matchups. We struggled with ball possession, which at times was very passive," said González. "My message to the players is I need everyone. In this case, we believed we needed to make some changes.

"This doesn't mean this is the team that's going to start the playoffs. Everyone shows me they're eager to want to play."

Messi doubled the score for Inter Miami, dribbling past defenders outside the box and smashing a trademark low, left-footed shot past Revs keeper Matt Turner.

The Revolution almost found their way back for a draw, but Ian Fray's own goal was quickly ruled offside to let Miami off the hook after it looked like Messi's heroics had been undone.

Ultimately, it was Messi's goal that clinched Inter Miami a spot in the 2027 Champions Cup. Had Miami lost or tied the game against the Revs they would have had work left to do on Decision Day on Nov. 7 to get into North America's top club competition.

"I have no doubt that he's the best of all," González said of Messi. None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues. Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or. I hope he can achieve it."

Inter Miami now joins Nashville SC, the Revs and the Vancouver Whitecaps in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. The winner of the 2026 MLS Cup will also have a place in the Champions Cup.

The Herons now have 59 points from 33 games, and will finish the regular season with a home game against Charlotte FC that will have seeding implications ahead of the MLS playoffs.

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: 'Do everything': Walsh credits Walters chat for return
stories.summary: Reece Walsh says it's "a blessing" to be a sponge around his Australia fullback competitor James Tedesco as he reveals how he got fit for the World Cup.
stories.body:
When Reece Walsh spoke to Australia coach Kevin Walters in August after ankle surgery concerning his World Cup hopes, there were no guarantees.

It is why the Kangaroos fullback's ice pack on his left ankle after the 66-6 win over Cook Islands on Saturday night, in his second man of the match display in the tournament, was a symbol of his commitment and drive beyond the flamboyance he shows on the field.

Walsh, 24, took a knock to the same ankle against the Aitu in Townsville that he suffered a high grade syndesmosis injury to while playing for Brisbane on August 15.

He played through the discomfort to set up five tries, vindicating all the hard yards in rehab that got him selected for his first World Cup.

"I spoke to Kevvie early and I said if you are thinking about picking me, I am going to do everything I can to get back," Walsh said

"He said, 'Walshy, nothing is guaranteed. If you get fit and get your ankle right I will have a look at it'. I didn't go on holidays. To be honest I worked really hard to put myself in a position to get back in this team."

Walsh spent three or four days at the Broncos with rehab and physio gurus such as Lindsay Self and Luke Anning, whom he praised for assisting him in their own holiday breaks.

They told him not to be overly concerned if he suffered a bump on the ankle.

"They generally say that when you have the tightrope (fixation surgery) and rod through it that it is stronger than it normally is," Walsh said.

"I was bound to get a bang on it. I didn't get one in the first game and I got one out there (against Cook Islands) so I feel like it was a good test of strength of it."

Walsh is in a fullback battle with Sydney Roosters captain James Tedesco, who was excellent in the 36-22 win over Fiji last week in the match Walsh did not play.

Walsh would widely be considered to have his nose slightly in front to play in the semi-final against Samoa at Allianz Stadium on Sunday night, but the coach has given him no indication.

"He actually hasn't. One thing we spoke about being in this environment and this team is nothing is guaranteed," Walsh said.

"We are all here to learn off each other and help each other get to the ultimate goal of winning the World Cup.

"Whatever Kevvie wants to do we are all going to support him. No one has dropped their lip or had a sour taste."

Walsh, also a Queensland representative, is a sponge taking in Tedesco's wisdom as he lives out his boyhood Kangaroos dream.

"When you look at this jersey I feel like it is the pinnacle of our game," he said.

"Origin level is so amazing but I also feel like as a kid you play in Queensland or NSW to make Australia.

"I wear that jersey with pride. I go out there to represent not just myself but our nation and my family and the people that set me up to be here.

"I feel like being in camp with Teddy has been such a blessing for me.

"To see someone like himself, the way he prepares, the way he carries himself and the character he is ... I am learning so much."
